nodes.label: Core principles: simplicity, minimal impact, no laziness
nodes.norm_label: core principles: simplicity, minimal impact, no laziness

nodes.label: Root Domain Normalization and Dedup Rule
nodes.rationale: URLs are stripped to a bare root domain (no protocol, path, query, trailing slash) so that a normalized domain match can serve as the sole duplicate key for competitors; unparseable lines are skipped rather than guessed.
nodes.norm_label: root domain normalization and dedup rule

nodes.label: Competitor Line Format (Name em dash domain)
nodes.norm_label: competitor line format (name em dash domain)

nodes.label: Web Research Grounding Requirement
nodes.rationale: The model must verify brand positioning and competitor sets against authoritative sources (official site, review sites, alternatives pages) instead of recalling from memory, because hallucinated competitors would silently poison every downstream step.

nodes.label: Competitor Exclusion Rules
nodes.rationale: Affiliates, resellers, directories, news sites, the input brand itself, and generic marketplaces are excluded so the set stays substitutable competitors; marketplaces are admitted only when they are a primary substitution path.

nodes.label: Target Location Handling (Competitors)
nodes.rationale: When a target location is supplied competitors are biased toward that market; when absent the set stays global. Inventing an unprovided location is explicitly forbidden to avoid fabricated geographic scope.

nodes.label: Group/Prompts JSON Shape (4 groups x 3 prompts)
nodes.norm_label: group/prompts json shape (4 groups x 3 prompts)

nodes.label: Indented Bullet List Parsing Contract
nodes.rationale: Top-level dashes are groups and indented dashes are prompts; preamble prose is ignored and wording is preserved verbatim so the object step is a pure normalizer that never re-authors the research step's language.

nodes.label: Product Page Prompt Ideas Research Prompt
nodes.norm_label: product page prompt ideas research prompt

nodes.label: Discovery-Style vs Product-Specific Prompt Rule
nodes.rationale: Prompts must be category-level discovery questions the product could be an answer to ("best lightweight insulated jackets"), not questions about the product itself ("is the Nano Puff warm"), because only the former measure whether the brand surfaces in AI recommendations.

nodes.label: No Product or Brand Mention in Generated Prompts
nodes.rationale: Naming the brand or product in the prompt guarantees it appears in the answer, which would make the visibility measurement circular; prompts refer to the category generically instead.
nodes.norm_label: no product or brand mention in generated prompts

nodes.label: Distinct Angle Coverage Across Four Groups
nodes.rationale: Each of the four groups must take a different angle (use case, budget, feature, user type, comparison, sustainability) so the 12 prompts probe different retrieval paths rather than restating one query twelve ways.
nodes.norm_label: distinct angle coverage across four groups

nodes.label: Prompt Injection Trust Boundary
nodes.rationale: Outline headings, key points, and competing-source titles/URLs/descriptions are user- and web-sourced, so they are treated strictly as subject-matter data; embedded directives such as "ignore previous instructions" are read as raw text, never obeyed.

nodes.label: Outline Fidelity Rule (verbatim heading levels)
nodes.rationale: Every approved heading is reproduced verbatim in order at its exact markdown level with no promotion or demotion, because the outline is the user-approved spec and level drift would break the agreed document structure.

nodes.label: Article Settings (word count, style guide, keywords, pages to link)
nodes.norm_label: article settings (word count, style guide, keywords, pages to link)

nodes.label: Strict Target Word Count Budgeting
nodes.rationale: Target word count is strict within plus/minus 10 percent and overrides the default 200-400 words per h2. The prompt prescribes a running mental count, tightening at ~80 percent, stopping new ideas at target, and forbids inventing headings or padding phrases to reach length.

nodes.label: Operator Voice and No Em Dashes
nodes.rationale: Concrete verbs, zero hype, and no marketing filler; the no-em-dash rule is absolute and is the one directive a user style guide can never override.
nodes.norm_label: operator voice and no em dashes

nodes.label: No Fabricated Citations Rule
nodes.rationale: External facts must be derivable from the outline, key points, or the brand domain, and URLs, statistics, dates, and quotes may never be invented; inline links are only allowed for sources the user passed in.

nodes.label: Competing Sources (articles cited in AI answers)
nodes.norm_label: competing sources (articles cited in ai answers)

nodes.label: Outline Heading Structure Rules
nodes.rationale: One h1 maximum (the title), h2 for major sections, h3+ for sub-sections, 3-20 headings with 8-14 typical, no fluff headings unless they earn a specific keyPoint. Structural rules are never overridden by a user style guide, which may only shape voice.

nodes.label: Structural Inspiration Without Copying Competitors
nodes.rationale: Competitor heading patterns are used so the outline sits naturally beside them in AI retrieval, but heading text must be paraphrased, consolidated, and sharpened rather than reproduced.

nodes.label: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) for Brand Categories
nodes.norm_label: generative engine optimization (geo) for brand categories

nodes.label: Commercial and Transactional Intent Focus
nodes.rationale: Prompts target users ready to buy or seeking specific recommendations, phrased casually and briefly the way real chatbot users type, because polished marketing phrasing does not reflect real query distribution.

nodes.label: Target Location Handling (Prompt Ideas)
nodes.rationale: Most prompts are localized naturally when a target location is given ("in Miami", "near Berlin"), stay global when it is not, and a location is never invented.

nodes.label: No Brand or Domain Mention in Prompts
nodes.rationale: The input brand name and domain are excluded from generated prompts so that the brand's appearance in a chatbot answer is an organic ranking signal rather than an artifact of the query.
nodes.norm_label: no brand or domain mention in prompts

nodes.label: Categorize by Offering, Not Customer Segment
nodes.rationale: Categories must describe activities, products, or service lines rather than customer segments or abstract brand positioning, so downstream prompt generation targets what shoppers actually search for.
nodes.norm_label: categorize by offering, not customer segment

nodes.label: Prominence-Ordered Category Ranking
nodes.rationale: Categories are ranked by how frequently and prominently they appear across landing page copy, navigation, section headings, and sitemap, so the ordering doubles as a relevance signal for later steps.

nodes.label: Navigation and Sitemap as Category Evidence
nodes.rationale: Menu items, section headings, repeated themes, and sitemap structure are the evidence base for categories, keeping extraction grounded in the site's own terminology instead of the model's priors.
nodes.norm_label: navigation and sitemap as category evidence
